dedupe_keys.name: summary agronomic data for crop model calibration and validation in sub saharan africa iita agwise and excellence in agronomy

description: A small table of crop parameters for calibrating and validating crop models for key crops in sub-Saharan Africa. The IITA data portal lists three downloadable CSV files: a data dictionary, a metadata sheet and the calibration table itself, which holds 60 rows for Ethiopia, Ghana, Kenya, Nigeria, Rwanda, Senegal, and Zambia, Malawi and Mozambique, across barley, cassava, common bean, maize, potato, rice, sorghum, soybean, teff and wheat. Each row gives a use case (for example the harmonised decision support tool, Kenya KALRO or Rwanda RAB), region, crop, maturity range, variety class, days to maturity, row spacing, plant population, water-limited yield, planting windows and a reference. The dataset was registered on 31 October 2024 by Siyabusa Mkuhlani, Vimbayi Chimonyo, Anton Urfels, Leidy Patricia Moreno Cadena and eight co-authors, free under CC BY 4.0, and the portal entry was last modified on 19 September 2025. Coverage is the listed countries and use cases. Caveats: values are summaries from literature and partner programmes, not field measurements, and the table is small. For simulation it gives the crop calendars and yield ceilings needed to set up DSSAT, APSIM or similar models for African food production, water demand and drought impact scenarios. Related catalogue records include DSSAT and the ICASA data standards.
